title: Jephthah
lead: The outcast son of a prostitute who was called home to lead Gilead against Ammon, argued Israel's case with a history lesson, vowed to offer up whatever came out of his house to meet him, and saw his only daughter come out dancing. He then fought a civil war against Ephraim at the fords of the Jordan.

sections.b: Jephthah's story (Judges 10:17–12:7) holds one of the hardest scenes in Scripture. Samuel names him among Israel's deliverers (1 Samuel 12:11), and Hebrews 11:32 lists him among the people of faith, without comment on the vow. The law forbids offering children (Leviticus 18:21; Deuteronomy 12:31), and the prophets condemn it (Jeremiah 7:31; Micah 6:7). Readers have long split over whether Jephthah's daughter was killed as a burnt offering or given to lifelong service at the sanctuary, and over whether the text approves, condemns, or simply mourns. The rabbis blamed both Jephthah and the high priest Phinehas, who could have released the vow (Genesis Rabbah 60:3; Leviticus Rabbah 37:4). "Shibboleth," the password at the Jordan fords (Judges 12:6), has become an English word for a test that marks who belongs.
